The core operator ARS_initial combines three independent sub-models: wellness, injury risk, and physical capability. Each component is weighted by learned coefficients w1, w2, w3, which are determined through supervised regression against expert ARS labels. This linear combination assumes additive independence among components, which may not hold under stress or fatigue. The style-adjustment factor w_style modifies ARS_initial based on aggressiveness score (ASP), penalizing high-exposure playing styles such as aggressive baseline play. This introduces a non-linear correction that reflects real-world load asymmetry. The system’s failure mode arises when expert labels are noisy or sparse, leading to misaligned weights. Additionally, the assumption of stable modalities (WHOOP, self-reports, video) breaks down during transitions or data loss. The injury risk classifier uses XGBoost to predict binary injury outcomes, while separate classifiers handle body regions. These classifiers must be calibrated to avoid overconfidence. Physical capability is inferred via MLP/LSTM on temporal physiological sequences. The integration process assumes these sub-models can be meaningfully combined linearly, which may fail if they are not conditionally independent or if their scales differ significantly. The system’s robustness depends on the consistency of expert labeling and the stability of input modalities.
